rationale: Path is a finite field-name list; classAt follows declared fields with [] returning the base. Entry positive/negative and ViewType className+entries implement the signed nominal view; whole is exactly the positive empty path, not another constructor. Entry.valid prohibits negative [] and invalid paths, entriesDisjoint rejects both prefix directions, duplicates included. Positive root versus no entries therefore remain distinct. The unit introduces rho,a,A,T and base before the observations used later; list representation stands for the explicitly nonoverlapping finite set.
limitations: Correspondence review compares prose, mathematics, definitions and theorem/example statements; Lean proof validity and command results are separate checks. Listing relevant source-context snapshots records definitions and assumptions consulted, not an audit of every tactic or unrelated declaration.

Finite-map notation uses the documented distinct-key and well-formedness conventions. Raw Lean list representations also admit malformed values; no functional-lookup or preservation claim is made for those outside the stated premises.
